topic_ko: 블록 파티에서 태어난 힙합 문화가 DJ Kool Herc의 브레이크 기법을 통해 브레이크댄스와 MCing으로 갈라져 나감

passage: Once the peace treaty held, rival gangs began throwing parties with one another instead of fighting.
Empty lots and deserted buildings turned into stages for gatherings called block parties.
Out of those gatherings grew a lively youth movement that people came to call hip-hop culture.
It rested on four pillars, and it pushed street violence aside in favor of music, dance, art, and style.
The parties thrown by DJ Kool Herc drew the biggest crowds of all.
By running two copies of one record on two turntables, he stretched the drum passage dancers loved most.
That stretched passage gave rise to circles of dancers who competed to show what they could do.
It also gave rise to the rhymed shouting over instrumentals that later became a role of its own.
choices: how hip-hop culture took shape at Bronx block parties
the technical challenge of operating two turntables at once
the reasons street gangs finally stopped fighting in New York
the contribution of graffiti artists to urban neighborhoods
the worldwide commercial success of modern rap music
theme.explanation_ko: 블록 파티에서 힙합 문화가 생겨나 DJing·브레이크댄스·MCing으로 뻗어 나가는 과정이 글 전체를 관통하므로 ①이 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ② 턴테이블 두 대는 언급되지만 그 '기술적 난이도'를 다루지 않는다. ③ 평화 협정은 첫 문장의 배경일 뿐이다. ④ 그래피티는 네 요소를 나열할 때 한 번 스칠 뿐이다. ⑤ 오늘날의 상업적 성공은 본문에 없다.

passage: With the fighting over, the gangs that had once attacked each other started celebrating side by side.
Vacant parking lots and empty buildings became the venues for events known as block parties.
What came out of them was an energetic youth movement built on DJing, breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti.
In place of gang violence, the neighborhood now had music, dance, art, and style.
DJ Kool Herc, later called the founding father of hip-hop, hosted the parties everyone wanted to attend.
His trick of switching between two identical records lengthened the drum break that dancers waited for.
Because the break never had to end, people formed circles and turned dancing into a contest of skill.
Meanwhile the rhymed shouting DJs used to fire up the crowd grew into a separate job of its own.
choices: 블록 파티에서 시작된 힙합 문화가 폭력을 대신하며 여러 갈래로 자라났다.
새로운 음향 장비의 발명이 대중음악의 흐름을 완전히 바꾸어 놓았다.
갱단의 폭력은 결국 더 강력한 단속을 통해서만 줄어들 수 있었다.
청소년에게는 무엇보다 안전한 실내 공연장을 마련해 주어야 한다.
그래피티는 도시 미관을 해치기보다 지역 정체성을 강화하는 예술이다.
gist.explanation_ko: 폭력의 자리를 음악·춤·예술이 채우며 블록 파티에서 힙합 문화가 여러 요소로 자라났다는 것이 글의 요지이므로 ①이 적절하다.
gist.distractor_ko: ② 장비 '발명'이 아니라 기존 턴테이블의 새로운 사용법이다. ③ 단속 강화는 언급이 없고 오히려 문화가 폭력을 대체했다. ④ 실내 공연장은 본문에 없다. ⑤ 그래피티에 대한 평가는 나오지 않는다.

passage: After the treaty, former enemies in the Bronx began holding parties together in the open air.
Abandoned lots and empty buildings hosted the events people called block parties.
From these parties came hip-hop culture, resting on DJing, breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti.
DJ Kool Herc, regarded as the founding father of hip-hop, hosted the most popular of them all.
At his sister's birthday party in August 1973 he tried something no one had done before.
Playing two copies of one record on two decks, he switched back and forth to stretch the drum break.
Dancers no longer had to stop, so they made circles and turned the break into a stage of their own.
DJs rhyming over the instrumental parts eventually handed that job to a friend, and MCing was born.

title.explanation_ko: 늘어난 브레이크 한 구간에서 DJing·브레이크댄스·MCing이 갈라져 나온 과정을 담아야 하므로 ①이 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ② 기법의 '대가'나 부담은 언급이 없다. ③ 파티가 금지되었다는 내용은 전혀 없다. ④ 그래피티는 전개되지 않는 요소이다. ⑤ 세계 시장 정복은 본문 범위 밖이다.

passage: After the treaty the old rivals began holding block parties in lots and empty buildings.
From those parties grew hip-hop culture, which put music and dance where violence had been.
DJ Kool Herc drew the largest crowds, and in August 1973 he tried a new technique.
Using two turntables at once, he switched between two copies of one record to stretch the break.
No longer did people have to stop dancing at the end of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc.
The break became the part of a song that everyone waited for.
Dancers formed circles and used it to display their own skills.
Herc called them B-Boys and B-Girls, short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls.
implication.underlined: No longer did people have to stop dancing at the end of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc.
choices: Herc's technique let the dancing continue without any break in the music.
Dancers were finally forbidden to stop moving during a party.
The DJ gave up changing records and played only one song all night.
People preferred resting between songs rather than dancing straight through.
Records became so long that no one noticed when they ended.
implication.explanation_ko: 같은 음반 두 장을 오가며 브레이크를 늘렸기 때문에 음악이 끊기지 않았고, 그래서 춤을 멈출 필요가 없어졌다는 뜻이므로 ①이 적절하다.
implication.distractor_ko: ② have to 의 부정은 '금지'가 아니라 '~할 필요가 없음'이다. ③ DJ는 오히려 두 장을 계속 오갔다. ④ 사람들이 쉬기를 원했다는 서술은 없다. ⑤ 음반 길이 자체가 늘어난 것이 아니라 브레이크를 이어 붙인 것이다.
